q1: What attracts me most to the baringa.ai Fellowship is the chance to apply AI to real client problems with experts around me. During my internship at DS Digital Technology, I designed a 246-question benchmark and a safety rubric to evaluate patient-facing AI answers for a pharmaceutical client, and built a Python pipeline that scored more than 2,400 responses from six LLMs. The client adopted the benchmark as its acceptance standard. That project showed me that the hardest part of applied AI is not building the model, but agreeing what good looks like and proving the system meets it. I want to keep doing this kind of work across different industries. The small cohort and the focus on technical depth, rather than years of experience, also suit me as a recent MSc graduate who wants to learn quickly from people at the top of their field.
q2: During my MSc at UCL, I enjoyed the research, especially my dissertation on cardiovascular risk using UK Biobank data. However, I realised the part I enjoyed most was when the analysis led to a decision, so I built a Streamlit tool to make the results usable for non-specialists. My internships confirmed this. At TikTok Shop UK, I used Claude Code to build an AI agent that automated a campaign configuration task and cut the time it took by around 40 to 50 percent. Seeing my team change how they worked was more rewarding than any single result. Consulting would let me bring the rigour I learned in research to many different problems, and work directly with the people who own them. I also like that I would keep learning new industries, rather than staying in one narrow topic.
